headline: Hormuz Crude Exports Threaten to Fall on Tanker Shortages as Brent Slides
summary: Crude exports from the Persian Gulf face potential declines due to an inbound tanker shortage, even as Brent crude prices slipped toward $92 per barrel from October peaks.
why: The Strait of Hormuz is the world's most critical oil transit chokepoint, where export disruptions directly affect global crude balances.

impacts.name: Brent crude
impacts.why: Brent crude prices slid toward $92 per barrel as Persian Gulf exports recovered toward pre-war levels.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Crude prices retreated as Persian Gulf export volumes recovered, though incoming tanker shortages threaten future supply flows.
